chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Miham, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is disliked to shorten the nails of the deceased, or shorten his hair, or shave off his pubic hair, or close down a joint of his.

key_terms.كُرِهَ: Disliked (makruh) - a juristic ruling indicating preference against an action but not strictly forbidden.

ai.seo_question: What grooming actions are disliked for the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the juristic preference (karahat) against grooming the deceased, reflecting the Shia view that the body remains in a state of ritual integrity after death. The specific prohibition of closing a joint (mufsal) highlights the concern for preserving the natural posture and dignity of the corpse, distinguishing these acts from the obligatory washing (ghusl) and shrouding (kafan).
